name: Pyrite
toxicityNote: Can release sulfur compounds when wet or heated; keep dry, avoid dust and do not make elixirs.
physical: Traditionally associated with vitality and stamina
Kept nearby for energy and drive
Linked by crystal healers to warmth and strength
summary: Pyrite is a brass-gold iron sulfide with perfect cubes and sunburst forms, the fool's gold used for confidence, willpower, and attracting abundance.
intro: Pyrite is the mineral that has fooled prospectors for centuries. Its brassy, metallic crystals form flawless cubes, pyritohedra with twelve faces and radiating discs called pyrite suns, and the shine on a fresh face can look like polished gold. It is hard enough to strike sparks from steel, 6 to 6.5, but brittle, and it can slowly tarnish or crumble if kept damp. Great cubes from Navajun in Spain look machine-made. Crystal lovers adore it for its glittering confidence, and it is one of the best-selling stones for prosperity.
history: The name comes from the Greek pyr, fire, because pyrite throws sparks when struck against steel or flint. Early firelighters and wheellock guns used it for ignition. Native peoples in Central America polished pyrite into mirrors, and it was carved into ornaments in Inca culture. The nickname fool's gold arose because gold rush prospectors mistook it for the real thing. Pyrite is also a source of sulfur and was used to produce sulfuric acid. In the Victorian era, marcasite jewelry made from pyrite was fashionable. In crystal practice it is a wealth stone.
meaning: Crystal healers see pyrite as a stone of confidence, willpower and abundance. It is linked to the solar plexus, and is said to energize ambition, protect against discouragement and attract success in work or money. Practitioners say it helps people stand up for themselves and keep going when a goal feels distant. Its mirror-like faces are also read as a shield, reflecting negativity. Emotionally it is tied to self-worth and an assertive but fair stance. Traditionally it is also associated with stamina and vitality, a warm drive in the body. Many keep pyrite near the cash register, desk or entrance to draw prosperity.
howToUse: Place a pyrite cube or cluster on your desk, in a business, or in the wealth corner of the home, the southeast. Hold a small piece before a negotiation or sales call to stay confident. Wear pyrite as a pendant for steady motivation, but keep it dry. In a grid, pair with citrine and green aventurine to emphasize prosperity. Pyrite suns make striking wall or shelf pieces and are often used as focus points for goal-setting.
care: Pyrite should be kept dry. Water, humidity and sweat can cause it to oxidize, releasing sulfur compounds and eventually crumbling in a process called pyrite disease. Wipe with a dry soft cloth and store in a cool, dry place with silica gel if you live in a humid area. Cleanse with sound, smoke or sun. Wash hands after handling and avoid breathing dust. Never make elixirs from pyrite.
identify: Genuine pyrite is brassy and hard, strikes sparks with steel, and leaves a greenish-black streak. Gold is much softer, buttery yellow, heavy and leaves a gold streak. Chalcopyrite is also gold but softer with iridescent tarnish. Fake pyrite cubes made of resin or painted glass exist. Genuine pyrite cubes show striations on faces, and sometimes grow into one another, while fakes are too perfect and light.

faq.q: Why is pyrite called fool's gold?
faq.a: Pyrite looks like gold at a glance, and prospectors often mistook it for the real thing. It is harder, more brittle and leaves a greenish-black streak instead of gold-yellow.
